answer: Each agent can earn the right to submit economic actions only by locking a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed horizon; a trellis of independent reviewers then checks sampled work, and a proven duplicate identity loses its stake. Creating many umber accounts no longer multiplies influence for free: the attacker must lock more capital per identity, keep it unavailable, and risk losing it when evidence of duplication appears. This raises the cost of a Sybil attack without assuming identities are impossible to fake.
